name: The binary El Farol: swings against the number of agents (CMO Fig. 1)
description: Challet, Marsili and Ottino's binary El Farol: 60 seats, strategies reading only whether recent weeks were crowded, each entry 'go' with probability 0.5; σ²/N over the last 100 of 5 000 rounds against the number of agents N, for memories 2, 3 and 6. At N = 120 agents want exactly 60 seats on average. Measured (release, seeds 1–10, recorded 2026-09-27): M 2 — 0.52, 0.11, 0.76, 1.34, 1.61, 1.61, 1.39, 1.17, 1.13 at N 80 to 160, worse than coin-flippers (0.24–0.25) near N = 120 and best at a bias (N 90); M 6 — 0.056 at N 120, better than coin-flippers, worse away from it. Short memories do worst where the strategies are unbiased; a longer memory turns that around, as they find.
